followed by a blank line, then in a contemporary hand: To gehadedum mannum. Us biscopum gedafenað i.e. Aelfric's pastoral letter ed. Thorpe Ancient laws 452.

note.label: Amen
note.seg: Besides differences already mentioned, the Latin adds details on church dues, mainly from II Edgar 2.2; a prohibition against selling men abroad (cf. V Ethelred 2) with an anathema on those who do; clauses on robbery, including the statement that the reeve who commits it is to pay double compensation; and a clause that every man, poor or rich, is to be entitled to law (cf. III Edgar 1.1).
